spans.text: ...Several hours ago.
In the command room at the Griffin base, back in reality.
After a few minutes of silence, Boys tries to keep her brow from furrowing and her voice calm.
Commander, I still think this plan is too risky. We simply know too little about Sector 2Z64, and Purin is our only source of information.
Purin's virus is indeed able to break the seal on the Dolls' memories, but I'm concerned about all the unforeseen problems we could encounter if we went in so ill-prepared.
I know, but this is urgent. We can't afford to wait any longer.
If you're discovered, you have the permission to withdraw immediately.
But...
Understood.
Knock, knock.
After knocking on the half-open door, Purin enters the command room with a box.
Since we're doing this, I'll share our key to victory with you~
Oh, stop looking so glum. The Commander is anxious to rescue the Dolls, and Boys is worried that the plan will fail because of the risks.
You are both working toward the same goal, so why are you at each other's throat?
I'm not. I'm just a bit tired and on edge.
I also don't mean to be insubordinate. Don't take this the wrong way.
Alright, alright, I'm mistaken.
C'mon, resources are in short supply, so we'll need to share this~
What's this?
Something that always comes in clutch whenever I find myself in a difficult predicament—
Purin opens the lid with a flourish.
Ta-daa! It's pudding!
Why aren't you even a little bit surprised?
Purin, you wasted five minutes just for a pudding?
This pudding is super important!
Ah, never mind. Just make sure both of you eat some!
Purin shoves a spoonful of pudding into Boys' mouth with exasperation.
Eat this, and our plan will go perfectly!
Do you believe me, Commander?
...Yes, I do.
She shoves another spoonful into the Commander's mouth.
Eat this, and promise you'll live a good life no matter what happens!
...In an old, deserted area in the Ministry of Truth, Sector 2Z64.
Following the Commander's plan, Boys successfully infiltrates Sector 2Z64 with Purin Esaki.
During Purin's previous infiltration, she has already created a false identity for herself in the system, so all she needs to do is meet up with 433 again.

While lying low at her hideout, Boys keeps trying to run simulations of how the plan will unfold, but due to insufficient data as well as limited sources of information, her simulations are inconclusive.
Commander, can Purin really be trusted?
Why would a stranger we've never met go so far for us?
Just as Boys' paranoia is about to spiral out of control, a sound can be heard from the end of the corridor.
This is a passage in a deserted part of the building. Hardly anyone would ever come this way.
It is indeed a secure location. We don't have to worry about being tracked.
Boys, come on out.
Boys peers out from her hiding place. Purin and a familiar figure are standing against the light. Their faces are obscured by shadow.
Are you No. 390 or 433?
I have recovered my memory.
Boys, is the Commander safe?
Yes.
Purin looks back and forth curiously at the two Dolls, who remain tense and motionless despite being clearly overcome with feelings.
This is supposed to be a touching reunion... Is that all you have to say to each other?
Cut the crap; what is the Commander's plan?
As an elite Doll, I've never had to ask about the operation plan in the middle of an operation...
The Commander believes that the abducted Dolls have their real memories sealed the way yours were.
Purin has created an "Alarm Clock" virus that can help the Dolls recover their memories. Our job is to make it spread as much as we can.
I remember when Purin infected me with the virus, it only took minutes for it to work...
If this virus is so effective, why don't we just infect each Doll as we come across them?
That's too slow. We'll only break the memory seal on a handful of Dolls, and Shimamura will be onto us.
Besides, every time we help a Doll, we'll have to explain the situation to her and make sure she is on board with the Commander's plan.
I doubt any Doll would refuse the Commander.
But it's undeniable that the Commander's plan is extremely risky. If we're discovered, there's no telling what awaits us.
It's true. There are too many variables in Sector 2Z64.
We can only take a gamble and try to unseal everyone's memories in one go and put an end to it all before Shimamura can stop us.
All in one go...
I see. That's why we need to get to the broadcast studio.
We can connect with all the Dolls from there.
Looks like I called it~
Sector 2Z64 conducts mandatory system-wide upgrades regularly. The next one will be later in the afternoon.
During the upgrade, all Dolls will be forced to connect with the broadcast studio to be vetted for the system upgrade.
So we'll make use of this opportunity, mix the "Alarm Clock" into the vetting process and send it out...
Wait, mandatory systemwide upgrades?
It's essentially a compulsory checkup to make sure there are no fatal loopholes or viral infections in the Dolls' system.
Sector 2Z64 is isolated from the outside, right? In this kind of vacuum, why would they...
Purin comes to an abrupt halt.
This could be their weakness.
Weakness?
It means that even with the memory seal, the Dolls' neural clouds are still unstable and require regular inspection.
That would certainly explain the system upgrades...
What if they fail the vetting process for the system upgrade?
According to Mizukane, they will be taken to Big Brother's room for repairs.
They will be released after passing the next system upgrade.
Repairs... That sounds really fishy.
Has anyone ever returned from such repairs?
Yes.
Just so you know, Miss 433, since you sound so self-assured... Before I broke your memory seal, more than half of your memories were fabricated.
Alright, I'm not absolutely certain, but I do remember a Doll who was taken away for failing the upgrade vetting process.
Then she came back after a few days, looking perfectly fine.
Who was it?
Ibis.
Ibis...
If we can find Ibis, we must ask her about Big Brother's room.
Big Brother's room... It's certainly a key location.
Sounds almost like a hidden boss room in video games.
Hush, we're here.
433 opens the door of the broadcast studio using a key, and the trio enter the room.
The playback freezes on this frame.
...Back in the present.
In an unknown area in Sector 2Z64.
The Major points at Purin in the simulation created from Boys' memory fragment.
She strokes her chin thoughtfully with a slight frown.
Up to this moment, things were still going according to plan.
What are you thinking, Major?
Esaki made quite an important observation here.
You mean the instability of the Dolls' neural clouds in Sector 2Z64 even with the memory seal?
Yes. She's as astute as ever, zeroing in on their weakness the moment she got here.
Big Brother's room is no doubt just as important. We don't have any information about it, but I believe it will prove crucial to a breakthrough.
Yeah, I agree.
The Commander redirects their attention to the simulation playback. Purin is still deep in thought.
Back then, you were clearly still...
So what made you change your mind?
Commander, I'm going to comb through the rest of Boys' memory fragments.
Okay.
...Several hours ago.
In the broadcast studio of the Ministry of Truth, Sector 2Z64.
As soon as the door opens, the gloomy, oppressive air spills out from within.
The dimly-lit room is jam-packed with flickering screens.
...There are so many surveillance cameras?
Yeah. All these feeds are transmitted from the telescreens.
The telescreens? Aren't those for communication?
What kind of communication port would have to be installed all over the place?
...Then could they have spotted us already?
Took you long enough to realize that, but luckily for you, I've been scrubbing us off the telescreen feeds along the way!
Beautifully done.
433 activates the broadcast system deftly.
I was tasked with broadcasting the system upgrade announcement this time.
The system upgrade will begin in ten minutes. We must complete our preparations by then.
Purin, please take care of the security system. Boys, help me with installing the "Alarm Clock" virus.
Sure.
Alright!
Hm? Wait, why are you just bossing me around like the Commander...
Purin mutters as she walks over to the security system operation terminal.
Without her constant jabbering, the entire broadcast studio is now silent.
Following the standard procedure, 433 sets up a broadcast to announce the upcoming system upgrade, while Boys prepares for the installation of the "Alarm Clock" virus.
Are you the only Doll at the base right now?
Yes.
Then you are the adjutant-on-duty.
How... how's the Commander doing?
They took it pretty hard, but they haven't lost hope yet.
The Commander is working out a way to rescue the abducted Dolls.
As an adjutant, your report can't be so ambiguous!

What do you mean, "took it pretty hard"? What were their exact bio indicators? Were you also monitoring their mental state? Keeping track of their nutritional intake? Have they been exercising regularly?
Such stalkerish behavior is unbecoming of a knight.
Then you're clearly slacking off!
When I get back, I'll strike your name off the next adjutant duty roster!
Do whatever you want when you get home.
...Stop giving me that look.
To tell you the truth, the Commander's mental health hasn't been the best lately. Their eating and sleeping schedule has also been rather erratic.
Probably due to their emotional state, even their command style has become much more aggressive.
Do you know what is bothering the Commander?
They didn't say anything explicitly, but I suspect they might be worried that the Dolls, deceived by this beautiful illusion, would refuse to return to reality.
If I had known, I would've told the Commander about it.
You mean the thing we're preparing?
What thing?
You know, our—
Hey, why are you eavesdropping on us?
You didn't seem to be having a secret conversation at such decibels.
You're done?
Yep, their security system is surprisingly backward. I sorted it out in minutes.
I even had a browse around their database, but I didn't find anything interesting, sadly.
Right, we're basically ready as well.
Three minutes until the system upgrade!
Should we start the activation process?
Yeah, let's do it.
433 finishes the final setup for the broadcast and turns on the microphone.
No. 390 here. All set.
Commencing broadcast of system upgrade.
The monitors all start showing the face of an avatar, and a cold, emotionless voice announces the start of the system upgrade.
What else do we need to do?
Just wait for the Dolls to connect to the system.
Click.
A comms request from the Commander.
Purin, Boys, I have located the Doll signals.
Commander, we are in the process of breaking the memory seal on the Dolls.
Good. I'm also attempting to retake command.
Understood! Remember to have the Major and Mr. Batou be your pathfinders.
The trio is just starting to feel a bit relieved when...
Pzzt... The line cuts out abruptly.
Commander?!
What's going on? Purin, are we getting signal fluctuations?
Purin's attention is drawn to the monitors.
...The "Alarm Clock" wasn't transmitted.
How is that possible?!
433 pulls up the backend logs to check the execution of their earlier command.
But no matter what she does, the monitors do not react. It is just the same face reading out the announcement emotionlessly.
Why isn't the system responding to my command?
The security system didn't register any errors... What is going on?
Can you force quit?
...I could, but that would draw attention to the broadcast studio immediately.
Should we risk it?
There are no alternatives. Do it.
433 opens the force quit terminal and presses the button without hesitation.
Pzzzzt! The ear-splitting noise almost shorted their neural clouds, but the impassive face remains on the monitors.
It didn't work!
Were they onto us all along? The system isn't acknowledging any of our commands...
Should we withdraw?
Pzzzzt! The noise is growing increasingly torturous.
Boys grabs 433's pale face and shouts at the top of her voice—
Get out of here, 433!
It's already...
All the exits have been sealed!
Too late...
What?!
Buy me some time. I'm gonna try—
Crackle—
The monitors showing the face suddenly emit a blinding flash.
Boys presses her palms against her eyes. Before she can react, another flash burns her eyes.
What is happening...?
Trapped in the room and assaulted continuously by what feels like countless flashbangs going off one after another, Boys and co. are utterly decapacitated.
Boys, watch out!
...What?
Miss Mizukane...
Hello, strangers.
Boys jumps in surprise, but it's already too late—
A soft hand is wrapped around her jaws.
The grip is gentle, as if it was just scratching a cat's chin, but Boys might as well have been struck by lightning.
Darkness obscures her vision, and the world melts away...
